chunks: Ahmad ibn Muhammad from al-Hasan ibn Ali ibn Yaqteen from his brother al-Husayn from his father Ali ibn Yaqteen from Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him) who said:
I asked him about the ship when its owner is unable to stand; should he pray while sitting, gesturing or prostrating? He said: 'He should stand, even if his back is bent.'

Muhammad ibn al-Hasan said: This report is understood to apply when he is able to stand; as for when he is not able to stand, it is permissible to restrict himself to praying while sitting and gesturing as we have clarified, and what was narrated also confirms this.
ai.seo_question: What is the ruling for prayer on a ship when one cannot stand?
ai.summary: This narration from Imam al-Rida (AS) establishes the principle of gradual ease in prayer, prioritizing standing even with significant physical compromise (bending the back) before resorting to sitting. Shaykh al-Tusi clarifies in his commentary that this ruling applies when standing is merely difficult; if standing becomes truly impossible, sitting with full gesturing is the valid alternative. This reflects the Shia juristic approach to 'rukhn' (excuse) based on the degree of incapacity.
